subject: Nebula Bios: VPC pilot concession and limited audit access request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nebulabios.com>
Date: 2027-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SOW and commercial summary for Nebula Bios VPC pilot
Attachments: SOW_NebulaBios_v1.pdf

Sanjay,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is the draft SOW for the 3-month VPC pilot we discussed plus a one-page commercial summary. Key bullets:
- Private VPC deployment in us-west with dedicated tenant isolation.
- Pilot term: 3 months, then option to convert to Dedicated.
- Standard pricing shown; inbound/outbound egress is included for the pilot.
- Customer requested 30% off list for first 12 months, plus limited audit access and a KMS escrow discussion.

From a delivery perspective, we can stand up the VPC pilot within 4 weeks once contract is signed. For the KMS ask, we typically offer customer-managed keys in Private but need legal alignment on escrow.

Please confirm the items you want in the SOW and any redlines. Happy to walk through this on a quick call.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nebulabios.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@nebulabios.com>
Date: 2027-09-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SOW and commercial summary for Nebula Bios VPC pilot
Attachments: Nebula_Compliance_Checklist.xlsx

Karthik,

Thanks for the SOW. A few asks from our compliance and procurement teams before we move:
- Commercial: We need 35% off list for year one to align with our pilot budget.
- Audit: We require the ability to perform a customer-led audit during the pilot window. We re looking for a 14-day access window, once during the pilot, to inspect logs and controls relevant to our data.
- KMS: Nebula prefers a KMS arrangement where keys are customer-controlled; if full escrow isnt feasible, we need a written guarantee that key material wont be exportable without our consent.
- Evidence: Please provide your latest SOC2 report and a short summary of logging retention policies.

We can be flexible on timing if we get legal language committing to the limited audit scope and residency.

Regards,
Sanjay Rao
VP, IT Operations
Nebula Bios
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-27T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nebula Bios asks - commercial concession and limited audit window (deal NB-2027-042)

Marissa/Laura,

Looping you in for deal desk and legal review. Customer is pushing for a 35% first-year concession and a one-off 14-day customer-led audit window during the 3-month pilot. Theyre also pressing for customer-controlled KMS or an escrow guarantee.

Summary of what I recommend:
- Approve a commercial concession up to 30% for year one to keep the pilot economics reasonable. Anything beyond that needs Bens sign-off.
- For audit: allow a single, scheduled 14-day read-only audit window limited to logs/controls scoped in an annex. Require an on-site or video-based review with Redwood security present. No access to host system consoles.
- KMS: offer customer-managed keys for Private but require assurances we can maintain backups and incident response. If escrow is needed, legal to propose language limiting use to lawful requests and with court-ordered process.

Risk notes: the audit and KMS asks increase legal exposure. Id prefer explicit indemnities and a short-term pilot carveout if we do this.

Can you advise next steps and whether this is approvable as a standard concession or needs exec sign-off?

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-28T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nebula Bios asks - commercial concession and limited audit window (deal NB-2027-042)

Karthik, Laura,

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick take from Deal Desk:
- Commercial: Standard playbook allows up to 25% off for pilots without C-Level approval. For 30%+, we need Ben Carter to sign the concession. 35% will require an exception memo and approval.
- Audit: We can accept a single 14-day read-only review limited to application logs and access logs, provided we attach a scoped annex that restricts collection and forbids host-level inspection. Security must be present and redact any PII unrelated to Nebula.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys are permissible for Private but require a technical gating checklist and additional onboarding fee to cover engineering support. No escrow unless Legal drafts strict usage controls.

Action items:
1) Ben to approve any concession >25%.
2) Laura to propose the audit annex language and KMS clause.
3) Karthik to communicate counter to the customer (recommend 30% + one-time onboarding fee).

Marissa
Sr Manager, Deal Desk
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-30T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nebula Bios concession request - conditional approval

Team,

After reviewing the ask and the risk mitigations, I approve a commercial concession at 30% for year one with the following conditions:
- Nebula pays a one-time onboarding and security review fee of $25k to cover engineering and compliance time.
- Audit window: one scheduled 14-day read-only audit during the pilot, scoped to application and access logs only, with Redwood security onsite/remote and a small set of agreed queries. No host-level access or KMS material may be requested.
- KMS: agree to customer-managed keys for Private, but no escrow. If Nebula insists on escrow, require a separate legal addendum and indemnity.
- SOC2: provide latest SOC2 report prior to signing; we will add the audit annex and a data residency clause for us-west in the SOW.

Laura, please draft the addendum and the annex reflecting the above and a one-time onboarding fee line in the order form. Karthik, relay to the customer that 35% is not approvable but we will do 30% under these conditions.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
